metadata.case_name: WAN CHUEN HOI v. WING SHUN ENGINEERING TRANSPORTATION LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: Truck driver responsible for transporting heavy machinery to construction sites
plaintiff.occupation_after: Driver/operator for Wong Tong (truck-mounted crane driver/operator); previously day-time driver and miscellaneous worker for Riseway

injuries.description: Trochanteric fracture of the left femur (fracture of neck of left femur / left hip fracture) with union and about 1cm shortening; metal implants in situ
source: X-ray revealed left distal radius fracture and trochanteric fracture of left femur.
x-ray showed fracture of neck of left femur.
For the left hip, the fracture had united in satisfactory position with about 1cm shortening of the fracture site.
Dr Lam opined that the implants for the left hip could be left in-situ and removal was not obligatory, but this could be a contributory cause of the residual pain with large movements of the hip.

injuries.description: Fracture of left distal radius and ulnar styloid (left wrist) treated with external fixation; probable intra-articular extension and non-union of ulnar styloid
source: x-ray showed fracture of left distal radius.
According to Dr Lam, the Plaintiff suffered trochanteric fracture of the left femur and fracture of left radius and ulnar styloid, which were consistent with the mechanism of the Accident.
For the left wrist, there was mild irregularity at the joint line (so it was probable that the initial fracture had an intra-articular extension) and non-union of the ulnar styloid.
There was mild residual tenderness over the dorsum of the wrist and mild weakness. There were 2 incision scars as a result of external fixation of the fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at other specified part of wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: Residual pain over left hip, which increased with climbing up and down, with squatting or with walking on uneven surface
Reduced walking and standing tolerance of up to 1 hour but requiring rest after 30 minutes; walked with a mild limp
Left thigh painful with every step; had to rest every 30 minutes; limited walking, sitting and standing tolerance
Could not carry heavy objects because his legs would not support the load
Mild residual weakness and stiffness of the left wrist
Pain on exertion and pain of the left wrist on stretching
Numbness over the dorsal aspect of left wrist and fingers
Mild irregularity at the wrist joint line consistent with probable intra-articular extension
Some stiffness and increase in pain for the left hip with prolonged activities (eg prolonged sitting/squatting and frequent climbing)

treatments_received: Ambulance to accident and emergency department and admission to orthopaedic ward
Close reduction and external fixation of left wrist (14 March 2006)
Open reduction and internal fixation with metal implants of left femur under general anaesthesia (14 March 2006)
Physiotherapy including inpatient rehabilitation (transferred to Tai Po Hospital for rehabilitation 6 to 30 April 2006) and outpatient physiotherapy

losses.description: Reduced walking, standing and sitting tolerance; walks with a limp; pain on climbing stairs and walking on uneven surfaces; needs frequent rest

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to carry heavy objects because legs will not support the load
Unemployed and dependent on comprehensive assistance since the Accident (as found in the EC Judgment)
Less agile and/or swift in his pre-Accident trade; difficulty returning to pre-Accident work requiring frequent climbing and physical agility
Residual pain, stiffness and weakness of left wrist and left hip following fractures and fixation
